chunks.content: ## Introduction to PBR Stickers in CLO2024.1 This section explains the concept of PBR (Physically Based Rendering) stickers, their role in material simulation, and the improvements made in CLO2024.1 for automatic generation of these stickers. PBR stickers define how surface properties interact with light and materials, enhancing realism in rendering. PBR stickers, also called physical stickers, are used to control how surfaces interact with simulated light and materials in physics-based rendering. They include various types such as physical graphics, simulation graphics, transparent graphics, surface roughness graphics, and metal graphics. These stickers influence the final visual appearance, making material performance more realistic and intuitive. Previously, generating PBR stickers in CLO required switching between CLO and Photoshop, complicating the workflow. The new version, CLO2024.1, introduces automatic generation of PBR stickers directly within CLO, streamlining the process. Users only need to prepare a four-sided continuous texture beforehand. --- ## Procedure for Automatically Generating PBR Stickers This section details the step-by-step process to generate PBR stickers automatically within CLO2024.1, including texture preparation, interface actions, and adjustable parameters. 1. **Texture Preparation:** Prepare a four-sided continuous texture as the base input. 2. **Material Selection:** In the Object window, select the desired material. 3. **Texture Assignment:** Add the prepared texture to the Property Editor. 4. **Automatic Generation:** On the backside of the discovery picture panel, locate and click the “Automatically Generate” button to create the PBR image. 5. **Adjust Intensity:** After generation, adjust the intensity of the PBR picture to refine the effect. 6. **Automatic Discovery Picture:** Similarly, use the automatic generation button on the back of the discovery picture to generate the discovery effect image. 7. **Smoothing Effects:** To make the discovery effect smoother and simulation more natural: - Open the Logic Editor. - Enable the Blur Edge function. - Adjust the blur radius accordingly. 8. **Simulation Picture Adjustment:** Modify particle diameter and simulation degree to optimize the simulation picture data. --- ## Generating PBR Stickers for Different Texture Types This section covers generating PBR stickers for various texture types, including transparent, surface roughness, simulation, and metal textures, along with customization options. - **Transparent and Surface Roughness Pictures:** These can be processed similarly by using the automatic generation function. - **Still Situation Appearance:** Supported primarily in lubrication materials due to compatibility with the Mikintree formula. - **Simulation Picture:** The simulation load data is integrated during automatic generation. Users can adjust simulation picture parameters and surface roughness data afterward. - **Metal Picture:** Open the Physical Editor for metal textures. Use the color switch to adjust black, white, and gray levels on the brightness side for desired metal reflections. --- ## Additional Features and Fine-tuning Options This section discusses other features for PBR sticker generation, including adjustments in the text editor, color optimization, and application to other object elements. - **Text Editor Adjustments:** After generating PBR stickers, open the Text Editor to adjust background color and achieve specific visual effects.

chunks.content: - **Metal Picture:** Open the Physical Editor for metal textures. Use the color switch to adjust black, white, and gray levels on the brightness side for desired metal reflections. --- ## Additional Features and Fine-tuning Options This section discusses other features for PBR sticker generation, including adjustments in the text editor, color optimization, and application to other object elements. - **Text Editor Adjustments:** After generating PBR stickers, open the Text Editor to adjust background color and achieve specific visual effects. - **Blurred Edge Control:** Adjust the blur radius for edge smoothing, then apply and disable the blur when satisfied. - **Rendering Review:** After adjustments, check the overall rendering effect for quality assurance. - **Additional Objects:** Besides materials and stickers, buttons, eyes, lines of sight, and accessories can also have PBR stickers automatically generated. - **Color Variations and Optimization:** Colors can vary based on user preference. CLO2024.1 supports color optimization tools to unify or customize colors across different elements. --- ## Color Modification Workflow This section explains how to modify colors of PBR stickers and apply changes using the application interface. - To change colors, select the object in the top-right corner of the image. - The color adjustment app will appear to the left of the information panel. - Use this app interface to move or change colors as desired, allowing for personalized color communication and optimization. --- ## Summary CLO2024.1 introduces a streamlined workflow for automatically generating PBR stickers directly within the software, removing the need for external tools like Photoshop. Users prepare a continuous texture and use built-in automatic generation buttons for various texture maps, including physical, simulation, transparent, roughness, and metal graphics. Adjustable parameters like blur radius, particle size, and color controls allow fine-tuning for realistic and visually appealing material rendering. The update also expands support to various objects beyond materials, such as buttons and accessories, enhancing the overall rendering workflow and customization options.
